text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.76% today after climbing nearly 2% yesterday to hit $399.44. The pullback comes as oil prices have retreated slightly from their recent highs—U.S. crude dipped to $97.26 a barrel today from above $100 just yesterday—while refineries continue running at 97.8% capacity. The near-term spike in oil prices drove the stock up over two weeks, but today's modest profit-taking and oil price easing reversed some of those gains.

The broader context matters here: refiners like Marathon benefit when crude and refined product prices rise, especially when they can run at high utilization rates like now. The Iran war has kept oil elevated and volatility high, which created the two-week rally, but energy markets are also pricing in political statements suggesting prices may stay elevated through the midterm elections—creating uncertainty about whether this price environment is sustainable.
